finding.summary: zte_touch_deinit called ufp_mac_exit before draining TPD report work, while report callbacks still check and later dereference ufp_tp_ops.pdev. Clearing that shared pointer at the start of teardown can race with an in-flight callback.
evidence: Stock Ghidra decompilation for zte_touch_deinit calls ufp_mac_exit before tpd_report_work_deinit.
The reconstructed syna_dev_process_touch_report callback checks ufp_tp_ops.pdev and subsequently loads ufp_tp_ops.pdev again for kobject_uevent_env.
The retained stock zte_touch_deinit body drains report/probe/resume work, removes proc/sysfs interfaces, and unregisters the child platform device after the early ufp_mac_exit call.

change.mechanism: ufp_mac_exit closes gesture admission, detaches and drains its workqueue, and removes the wakeup source while preserving the platform-device pointer. A C wrapper invokes the retained exact stock zte_touch_deinit body; after its report-work drain, interface removal, and platform-device unregister complete, the wrapper clears the pointer under the lifecycle mutex.
teardown_order: close gesture-report admission under the UFP lifecycle mutex and clear the gesture workqueue slot
cancel and drain delayed gesture work; destroy its queue and remove the wakeup source
execute the retained stock zte_touch_deinit body, including report/probe/resume work cancellation and interface removal
after the stock body returns, clear ufp_tp_ops.pdev under the lifecycle mutex
change.race_property: TPD paths that test and dereference ufp_tp_ops.pdev during stock teardown continue to see the still-registered device until the stock teardown has drained its built-in report work and removed interfaces. Gesture reporting is separately gated before its queue is destroyed.
change.retained_stock_body: The zte_touch_deinit AArch64 instruction stream is retained under zte_touch_deinit_stock_exact; only the symbol label/size name changed.

limits: Canonical Docker build and byte reproducibility passed; runtime scheduler behavior and NX809J hot-unbind/hardware teardown were not exercised.
The pointer remains available through the retained stock teardown and is cleared immediately after it returns; external platform/event callback behavior remains subject to runtime validation.
